title: Mexicana Expects to Reach Profitability Starting in 2030
author: Darylh Rodríguez
content:
_This article by[Darylh Rodríguez](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/darylh/)
originally appeared in the [October 8, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/mexicana-de-aviacion-
preve-alcanzar-rentabilidad-a-partir-de-2030/), an investigative Mexican news
outlet._

The state-owned airline **Mexicana de Aviación** expects to reach its **break-
even point starting in 2030** , when it also hopes to achieve
**profitability** , according to its strategic growth plan. The strategy
contemplates expanding its fleet, currently made up of 10 aircraft,
consolidating its operations and strengthening its flight offerings.

During the morning press conference of President **Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo**
this October 8, the director general of Mexicana de Aviación, **Leobardo Ávila
Bojórquez** , reported that the company is in a **first stage of capacity
integration**. He explained that this year five Embraer E2 aircraft were
incorporated, two of which are still in the “**certification process** ”
before the aeronautical authority.

“This has allowed us, **starting in the month of June, to increase our seat
offering by 83 percent so far this 2026**. This seat offering has allowed us,
precisely, to serve the different markets, the different destinations to which
Mexicana is flying,” he stated.

The executive detailed that the strategic plan contemplates **three stages**.
In the first, the airline expects to close 2026 with 12 aircraft and
incorporate eight additional ones during **2027** , with which it would reach
a fleet of **20 airplanes**. The second, of maturation and consolidation of
operations, would begin in 2028. For the third, starting in 2030, it projects
reaching the break-even point and profitability.

As for its results, he reported that the **number of passengers transported
increased 31 percent so far this year** , compared with the same period of
2025. Since the start of operations, the airline has carried more than
**1,276,000 passengers**.

Through **Mexicana Cargo Services** , the company has moved more than **1,314
tons of cargo**. Separately, Ávila Bojórquez reported growth of **23 percent**
in cargo transport during 2026, compared with the same period of the previous
year. He also highlighted the alliance with Correos de México to offer
logistics services.

During 2026, Mexicana added flights to **Acapulco, Guerrero; Tuxtla Gutiérrez,
Chiapas; Chihuahua; Hermosillo and the Bajío**. In addition, starting
**November 17** it will begin operating the route between Felipe Ángeles
International Airport (AIFA) and **Zacatecas**. For the winter season, it
plans 24 additional flights to Tulum, Quintana Roo.

### **More Jobs Linked to the Operation**

Ávila Bojórquez noted that the airline’s growth has also generated jobs
related to the aeronautical sector. According to his figures, the company has
generated **more than 840 direct jobs and more than 7,200 indirect ones**.

During Claudia Sheinbaum’s conference, the executive explained that the
airline’s plan rests on four pillars: efficiency and operational safety;
orderly, efficient and sustainable growth; compliance with aeronautical and
administrative regulations; and **environmental sustainability**.
